name: The Beacon (Persistence and C2 Detection)
description: Malware analysis lab on persistence and command-and-control (C2) detection. A single victim VM, base-provisioned here with tcpdump/net-tools and a static IP; a real Cobalt Strike Beacon implant is deployed and persisted (cron or systemd timer) manually afterward, then the analyst investigates it cold: find the persistence mechanism, triage the payload with file/strings, and catch the periodic C2 check-in with netstat/tcpdump. 'attacker' is your own existing, independently-licensed Kali + Cobalt Strike team server VM, expected at 192.168.150.20 on this same network segment -- not provisioned or touched by LabForge; point its network adapter at 192.168.150.0/24. See docs/labs/the-beacon.md for the manual VMware network-isolation step, the exact vmrun snapshot/revert commands for the clean-baseline and post-deployment snapshots (LabForge has no snapshot automation for any provider), and the exercise.

attack_tags.note: Beacon execution scheduled via cron or a systemd timer, wired up manually after this VM is provisioned
Cobalt Strike Beacon check-in to the team server on a long, predictable sleep/jitter interval
